transcript:
Meeting Header: 2027-05-28 10:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Nexa EM), Carlos Ruiz (Nexa ML Eng), Tara Nguyen (Nexa Security), Liam O'Connor (Nexa Network)

[00:00] Alex Kim: Morning everyone, thanks for jumping on a day later than usual. agenda: quick access check, results from the small runs Jordan kicked off, network, security, and actions.

[00:20] Priya Sharma: Sounds good. Quick status on our side: Carlos pushed a bucket ACL change earlier this morning, should allow the Redwood service account to list now. Carlos, you want to confirm?

[00:28] Carlos Ruiz: Yeah, I just tested with the ARN Jordan sent, and the list call succeeds; there was a miss on the assume-role policy. I'll paste the sanitized path to the trace folder in the chat after this.

[00:38] Jordan Patel: Great, thanks. I already started a couple of short runs using the sample traces  and the baseline looks consistent with last time: med ~200ms, p95 ~560-600ms on hosted with default batching. Enabling prefix KV cache brought median down by ~18% for repeated flows.

[00:58] Maya Lopez: Note on batching: we tried batch size 4 and 8; batch=4 gave better p95 but lower throughput; batch=8 increased throughput but bumped median a bit. We'll include the tradeoff table.

[01:18] Priya Sharma: For the product team p95 near 600ms might be too high for some interactive features. We discussed dedicated earlier; can you give a rough delta if we move to dedicated GPU pool?

[01:28] Jordan Patel: From our bench, dedicated reduces queuing so p95 can drop by ~25-40% depending on model and concurrency. Also with dedicated we can pin optimized kernels and choose quantization profiles safely. We'll show a projection in the sheet.

[01:45] Tara Nguyen: On KMS and encryption, will Redwood need decrypt permissions on our CMK or can you operate with encrypted payloads only? detail matters for our compliance team.

[01:54] Jordan Patel: Typically for POC we can accept encrypted payloads and work with a scoped CMK that allows Redwood service account decrypt for model inputs if needed. We support customer-managed KMS; we'll document the exact IAM role perms in the security pack.

[02:10] Liam O'Connor: Regarding VPC peering, the network team asked for specific ports and health check IPs. Jordan, can you send a minimal diagram?

[02:18] Jordan Patel: Yep I'll send an architecture diagram and a small list: outbound gRPC on port 443, healthcheck from our control plane ip range, and the CIDR we'll peer from. We'll include the TCP/UDP rules needed.

[02:30] Alex Kim: We'll also propose a narrow peering approach to minimize blast radius  ephemeral public egress only where necessary.

[02:42] Priya Sharma: For the quantization A/B we need confidence that hallucination doesn't spike. Can you run the A/B on our sanitized prompt set?

[02:50] Jordan Patel: Yes, we can. Plan: run the same prompts through fp16 baseline and 4-bit quant, compute the eval metrics you provided (truth labels + quality score), and surface diffs. If regressions exceed your threshold we can configure route-level fallback to fp16.

[03:12] Carlos Ruiz: How long will the A/B runs take? we want results before the benchmark start.

[03:18] Jordan Patel: Should be within 5 working days once we have the sanitized prompts and S3 path; aiming to post by 6/4.

[03:30] Maya Lopez: Also quick note: we can instrument request-level traces and export them to your SIEM; if you want token-level cost per request we can provide that too.

[03:42] Tara Nguyen: Good. We'll need retention options for logs and assurance on redaction. Please include that in the security pack.

[03:50] Alex Kim: We'll include retention mapping, redaction configs, and sample audit entries.

[04:05] Priya Sharma: Liam, any infra blockers for peering?

[04:10] Liam O'Connor: main question is NAT and egress rules; we will need the specific peering CIDR and a contact from Redwood to run the firewall changes. I'll be the contact.

[04:18] Alex Kim: Great, adding Liam to the action items. Jordan and Maya will prepare the diagram and send it.

[04:30] Priya Sharma: Another item: region pinning  some data must remain in EU. Can Redwood run the pilot in eu-west-1?

[04:36] Jordan Patel: Yes we can run the pilot in eu-west-1 for the EU traces; we'll include region-specific cost/latency estimates. For Dedicated we'll provision capacity in that region.

[04:50] Carlos Ruiz: One more on observability: can we get a live dashboard during the benchmark? product team wants a view of p50/p95, error rates, and cost burn.

[04:58] Maya Lopez: Yes, we can provide a shared dashboard and grant read-only access for the trial. We'll prepare that before the 3-day run.

[05:12] Tara Nguyen: On legal, I'll send an NDA addendum about POC data handling later today. please confirm you can accept that.

[05:18] Alex Kim: We'll review it and confirm.

[05:30] Priya Sharma: Ok to recap: Carlos will confirm S3 path and paste sample traces, Liam to share subnet/CIDR and firewall contact, Tara to send NDA addendum, Jordan to run KV cache tests and A/B quant, Alex to update benchmark sheet and send security pack. Follow-up sync on 6/10.

[05:48] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the spreadsheet, diagram, and security pack by Friday.

[06:00] (goodbyes and small talk)

End of transcript.
